notes.dir: For likert5 questions, dir=1 means higher agreement increases the trait score; dir=-1 reverses it.

types.likert5: Five-point agreement scale. Shared options are also copied into each likert5 question.
types.scale3: Single-choice categorical scale. Some questions have more than three options despite this type name.
types.knowledge: Single-choice knowledge question with correct flags and explanation.
types.multi: Multi-select question. noneValue marks the mutually exclusive none option.

notes.targets: Each question has one or more scoring targets selected from prompt.py TRAIT_DESCRIPTIONS. dir=1 means higher answer value indicates a higher level of that trait; dir=-1 means reverse; weight expresses relative contribution within the question.
notes.legacy_fields: section, trait, and dir are kept as compatibility fields and mirror the first target.

questions.text: On average, how much time do you spend online each day using a phone, tablet, or computer?
questions.context: Include social media, web browsing, app use, and similar activities.

questions.text: Overall, how active are you on social media?
questions.context: For example, Weibo, WeChat Moments, Facebook, or Instagram.

options.label: Rarely active (infrequent use, with little posting or interaction)
Occasionally active (a few times a week, with some interaction)
Frequently active (multiple times a day, actively posting and interacting)

questions.text: If a website uses cookies, this means it can…

options.label: View files saved on your computer
Track your visits and activity on that website

questions.explanation: Cookies are small files that websites store in your browser, primarily to track browsing behavior and preferences.

questions.text: What is a deepfake?

options.label: An AI-generated image, video, or audio recording that appears real but depicts something that did not actually happen
A text-based chatbot that makes people think they are talking to a real person
A system for recording and protecting information online
A program that makes users appear to access the internet from a different location

questions.explanation: Deepfakes use generative adversarial networks (GANs) to create highly realistic fake media and pose a significant threat to privacy and information security.

questions.text: How do large language models, such as ChatGPT, generate responses?

options.label: Generate sentences randomly by rearranging keywords from the question
Search the internet and summarize relevant results
Generate responses based on word patterns and relationships learned from large amounts of online text
Use preset responses and fill them with keywords from the question

questions.explanation: LLMs learn statistical patterns from large amounts of text and, during inference, use the context to generate the most probable next word.

questions.text: When a website has a privacy policy, this means the website…

options.label: Has entered into an agreement with users about how it uses their data
Will not share personal information with third parties
Complies with federal guidelines on deceptive advertising
Will not retain any personally identifiable information

questions.explanation: A privacy policy is a legal statement explaining how a platform handles data; it is not a promise to protect that data.

questions.text: When you browse in incognito mode on a work computer, which group will not be able to see your browsing activity?

options.label: The IT department that manages the company network
The internet service provider used by the company
Coworkers who use the same computer

questions.explanation: Incognito mode only prevents browsing history from being saved on the local device. The IT department, internet service provider, and websites you visit can still see your activity.

questions.text: What is end-to-end encryption?

options.label: Only the sender and recipient can read the message
Anyone on the network can read the message
The service provider can always read the message

questions.explanation: End-to-end encryption encrypts a message on the sending device and decrypts it only on the receiving device, so even the service provider cannot read it.

questions.text: What is browser fingerprinting?

options.label: A method of identifying users through browser or device settings and characteristics
A way to delete all cookies from a browser
A tool that encrypts all website traffic
A feature that blocks pop-up advertisements

questions.explanation: Even after you clear cookies or use incognito mode, websites can combine details such as your browser version, fonts, and screen resolution into a unique fingerprint to track you.

five_person_traits.openness: The tendency to be curious, imaginative, and open to new apps and services.
five_person_traits.conscientiousness: Tendency to regularly check account security settings and manage passwords systematically
five_person_traits.extraversion: Tendency to share personal information, experiences, and location openly on social platforms
five_person_traits.agreeableness: Tendency to comply with data collection requests or grant permissions to avoid friction or conflict
five_person_traits.neuroticism: Tendency to overreact to security alerts or, conversely, to avoid engaging with them due to anxiety

attitudes_and_perceptions.privacy_concern: Overall level of concern regarding privacy and security issues
attitudes_and_perceptions.data_concerns: The degree of concern about the collection, storage, or misuse of their personal data
attitudes_and_perceptions.online_trust: Trust in websites, including the reliability of their information and their handling of personal data
attitudes_and_perceptions.home_network_trust: The degree of trust in home Wi-Fi/network security
attitudes_and_perceptions.data_collecting_entity_trust: The degree of trust in entities that collect personal data (e.g., apps, platforms, and service providers)
attitudes_and_perceptions.threat_source: Perception of whether security threats originate locally or remotely
attitudes_and_perceptions.privacy_protection_actions: Whether users believe that privacy protection measures or actions are necessary
attitudes_and_perceptions.attitudes_toward_being_monitored: Concern about being monitored or tracked, especially regarding the collection and tracking of personal data
attitudes_and_perceptions.security_vs_convenience: Preference for security versus convenience, affecting whether you prioritize safety or ease of use in decisions involving personal data
attitudes_and_perceptions.social_vs_privacy: Trade-off between social needs and privacy protection

knowledge_and_learning.sources_of_security_knowledge: Primary channels through which security knowledge is acquired
knowledge_and_learning.types_of_perceived_threats: Types of threats the user consciously recognizes as personally relevant

behaviors_and_practices.daily_online_hours: Average daily online time across all devices (hours)
behaviors_and_practices.social_networking_use: Frequency and depth of social networking engagement
behaviors_and_practices.ability_to_help_others: Demonstrated capacity to diagnose and resolve security/privacy issues for others
behaviors_and_practices.behavior_changes: Magnitude of behavioral change following a security incident or warning
behaviors_and_practices.initiative_on_reviewing_policies: Self-initiated frequency of reading privacy policies or ToS before consent
behaviors_and_practices.proactive_or_reactive: Security posture orientation: proactive (preemptive hardening, hygiene routines) vs. reactive (responds only after incidents or external prompts)
behaviors_and_practices.tendency_to_adjust_website_settings: Tendency to adjust default website/browser privacy settings
behaviors_and_practices.password_layer: Diversity of password security levels (weak/strong/multi-level across account sensitivity tiers)
behaviors_and_practices.tendency_to_censor_information: Tendency to selectively omit, obfuscate, or withhold personal data
behaviors_and_practices.completeness_of_fallback_authentication: Coverage and robustness of account recovery mechanisms
behaviors_and_practices.number_of_passwords: Count of distinct passwords actively in use across accounts
behaviors_and_practices.recording_passwords: Method and security of password storage
